source.title: Implicit Regularization Towards Rank Minimization in ReLU Networks
source.authors: N. Timor; Gal Vardi; Ohad Shamir

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically and theoretically challenges simple rank-minimization accounts of implicit regularization in shallow ReLU networks, while qualifying the account with positive results for sufficiently deep networks. It does not measure train–test generalization gaps directly.
record.gate_note: The paper studies implicit bias toward low-rank weights, not the listed train–test generalization outcomes. Its own relevant results are about rank measures and optimization behavior; the generalization statements in the introduction cite prior work and are not this paper's results. The shallow-network rank results are captured as rows for the nearest mapped version, V7, but they do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap relation.
record.test_reason: The study tests implicit bias toward low-rank weights, not any listed claim version. Its rank theorems and toy experiment measure neither held-out performance nor magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps. Generalization findings appear as cited motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: shallow ReLU gradient flow need not minimize exact or approximate weight rank, while sufficiently deep networks admit conditional low-rank-surrogate guarantees at global minimum-norm interpolating or margin-optimal solutions. These guarantees do not establish generalization performance; convergence to a classification KKT point alone is insufficient for the global-optimum guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes gradient flow and rank surrogates in fully connected ReLU networks; the listed versions concern test error, train–test generalization gaps, optimizers, batch sizes, dropout, sharpness, and memorized-example removal. The paper does not test those generalization outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and training objective/solution condition change the rank-related conclusions: shallow depth-2 networks have negative rank-minimization results; deeper networks have positive conditional bounds. The empirical shallow result also depends on initialization and dataset geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Small-initialization gradient flow in depth-2 width-2 ReLU networks can converge to full-rank first-layer weights despite an available rank-1 interpolating solution. In the experiment, all 79 successful runs had stable ranks described as bounded away from 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient flow need not minimize exact or approximate weight rank in shallow ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: For sufficiently deep networks, global minimum-parameter-norm interpolants with nonnegative scalar targets satisfy bounds driving an aggregate rank surrogate toward 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth can enforce low aggregate rank surrogates at globally minimum-norm ReLU interpolants.

fits_no_version.finding: Global minimum-norm margin-1 classifiers satisfy depth-dependent rank-surrogate bounds; the harmonic mean of Frobenius-to-spectral norm ratios approaches an upper bound of sqrt(2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficient depth constrains aggregate rank surrogates at globally optimal parameter-margin solutions.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Algorithmic Learning Theory (2022)
record.problems: The paper does not measure train–test error or generalization. The empirical shallow-network experiment uses only a two-example toy dataset and reports a qualitative histogram rather than exact stable-rank values. The deeper-network conclusions are conditional on global minimum-norm or margin-optimal solutions; the paper notes that the square-loss gradient flow is not known to be biased toward minimum-ℓ₂-norm solutions.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows omitted. Cited prior findings about generalization and compression are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps, and its ranking performance relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 classification and V7 links confuse rank minimization with the distinct sharpness–generalization claim. No listed version receives a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels alongside generalization on natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on image tasks.
Held-out performance of adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers.

The study examines rank-related properties of trained networks but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gaps, or compare sharpness rankings against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: depth-2 width-2 ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow on square loss from a sufficiently small initialization; theorem concerns convergence to zero-loss solutions.

conditions.value: two inputs and two linearly independent unit target vectors in R²
each incoming and outgoing weight vector norm less than stated bound

rows.measure: rank of first-layer weight matrix W at convergence
rows.value: rank(W(∞)) = 2, if gradient flow converges to a zero-loss solution
rows.note: This is an implicit-bias/rank result, not a measurement of sharpness or generalization gap.
rows.check: The rank-2 theorem concerns failure of rank minimization, not a reversal of V7. It measures neither sharpness nor generalization gaps.

rows.subject: depth-2 width-2 ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent used to simulate gradient flow for 3·10⁶ epochs at step size 10⁻⁴.

conditions.value: two points; targets are standard basis vectors; inputs are normalized (1, 0.99) and (−1, 0.99)
rows of W(1) and columns of W(2) sampled uniformly from sphere of radius 10⁻⁴ around origin

rows.measure: stable numerical ranks of weight matrices among runs converging to negligible loss (<10⁻⁴)
rows.baseline: Rank 1 is the low-rank reference discussed in the text
rows.value: 79 runs converged to negligible loss; resulting stable ranks are described as rank 2 and not close to low-rank
rows.note: The text characterizes the histogram but gives no exact stable-rank values. The 79/288 count is stated; the rank outcome is described qualitatively.
rows.check: Stable rank does not measure V7. Only the 79 of 288 runs reaching loss below 10^-4 enter the reported histogram. Exact rank 2 should not be presented as an exact stable-rank value; stable ranks are described qualitatively as bounded away from 1.
